page0.text:
...
I couldn't do anything, even if I wanted to. I know that.
But even now...I can still feel her hand in mine.
I told her we should do our best.
She shook my hand when I offered it.
So...

page1.text:
"Agh, well isn't that obvious...!!"
If I climb up this hill and chase after the giant, I'll be killed.
I suppress a tremble and sprint up the hill as fast as I can.

page2.text:
"Saber...!"
I run into the barren land.
...And then.
What I see defies all expectation.

page3.text:
A tombstone goes flying.
Every time the giant roars and swings his massive sword, he splits tombstones in two.
In the midst of that...
...a knight dashes, undaunted, through the storm of tombstones.

page4.text:
That monstrous cleaver weaves a raging storm around the giant.
Tombstones crash together in a deafening cacophony.
In the center of that storm, Saber fights Berserker, matching his power—if not exceeding it.

page5.text:
...
""
Their positions have reversed.
She's using her much smaller size to her advantage.
Berserker is so large that he's hindered by all the obstacles around them.
Saber is able to move around freely, darting between them.

page6.text:
These obstacles are trivial to something as strong as Berserker...
...but it's more than nothing.
It's a small advantage, but in a battle like this, even that small advantage is tipping the balance in the other direction now—

page7.text:
"Over here...! You're in the way!"
"Huh? Woah...!?"
"What are you thinking!? Didn't I tell you to run? Are you deaf?"
She is absolutely fuming.

page8.text: "I...heard you, but I can't just run away, right?"

page9.text: "What!? How did you figure that!? Don't you get it? You can't fight! You're just in the way here! If you died trying to make a difference, well, that happens. But if you're killed before you can even do anything, you'll be dying in vain!"

page10.text:
"...?"
...I don't know why, but Tohsaka is furious.
Weirdly, I'm not upset about how she's yelling at me.

page11.text:
"Hey. Is that really something for you to get mad about? If I die, even in vain, it's not really your problem, is it, Tohsaka?"
"It has everything to do with me! It bothers me if you don't get home safely even when I'm letting you go for the day!"

page12.text:
"..."
...And now I'm even more confused.
Tohsaka really puts up a front at school.

page13.text:
"Geez. Anyway, you're not hurt, so just run away."
...That llyasviel brat really does seem to be planning to kill us all."

page14.text: "I know that. But I'm not running away. Saber is still fighting, and I won't leave her."

page15.text:
"...That's what an experienced Master should say. The problem is, you're going to die in vain since you can't do anything to support her.
This is your last chance. Go on now."
"No way. There has to be something I can do as long as I'm alive. Plus, Tohsaka, would you make someone else do something you can't?"

page16.text:
...
Tohsaka stares at me, her expression serious.
"...You're right. It was wrong of me to force something I can't do onto you."

page17.text:
She looks away.
"...Well, you might not even need to run away. It doesn't look like Saber's going to lose now."
Tohsaka peers at the cemetery from behind a tree.

page18.text:
Their battle continues, unchanged.
Berserker's attacks slash only empty air, tearing apart his surroundings like a tornado.

page19.text:
Between those attacks...
...within the swirling whirlwind and flying clods...
...and rain of broken tombstones...
Saber steps in closer to Berserker and attacks, without even scratching her armor.

page20.text:
"..."
This is...divine. Like nothing I've ever seen.
After witnessing a battle that is nearly impossible for humans, the fear I felt until just now disappears.
In fact, I'm fascinated.

page21.text:
The whole thing about the Holy Grail War hadn't really sunk in yet, and I was so anxious.
But after seeing her? All that just...fades away.

page22.text:
Swords dance around each other in violent, brutal arcs.
At the center of that whirlwind of fatal destruction, the knight challenges her enemy without hesitation.

page23.text:
Maybe this is what made me accept it all.
No matter what may wait in the future...
...with Saber at my side, I could fight even a god.

page24.text:
"...I thought so. I thought it was suspicious, but she blocked Berserker's sword on purpose."
Quietly...
Tohsaka mutters without emotion.

page25.text:
"...Was that to lure Berserker here?"
"Figured it out too, huh. Fighting that thing in the open, with no cover, is suicide. So Saber chose this place as their battlefield. She did it cleverly, too, drawing Berserker away from you while pretending to be on the back foot."

page26.text:
...
...That would mean...
Saber must have decided this was a good place to fight as far back as when we were walking down the hill.

page27.text:
"Certainly, you can't expect backup in a battle like this.
But this monster nullifies even Archer's arrows.
Backup would've been meaningless in the first place."
Tohsaka mutters while watching the battle between Saber and Berserker.

page28.text:
"...Archer's arrows..."
Those words get my attention.
Archer is nowhere to be seen.
If he is a bowman as his name suggests, then close combat probably isn't his thing, but...

page29.text:
"She got him...!"
Tohsaka snaps her fingers.
Just as she said, either Saber must have struck Berserker, or he must have lost his footing...
Berserker, who hadn't so much as faltered until now, loses his balance.

page30.text:
""
He unleashes a wild attack in desperation.
Saber dodges backward and grips her sword with both hands.

page31.text:
...This is it.
As his desperate attack is dodged, Berserker loses his balance completely...
...and Saber bends her knees to rush in with all her might.

page32.text:
Then...
"...Huh, Archer...? What do you mean 'get away'?"
I notice the confusion in Tohsaka's voice as she tilts her head. Then I sense the lethal intent aimed in this direction...from far away.

page33.text:
...
From behind.
I see a knight in red holding a bow on a rooftop hundreds of meters away.

page34.text:
...
It's either nausea or chills.
He's holding a bow.
It's no different from before.
Even if he aims perfectly, it won't do any damage.
So there's no sense feeling so threatened by it...

page35.text:
...
...but I get chills anyway.
He's nocked...it's not an arrow. It's something else.
That intent to kill isn't directed solely at Berserker.
